record.original_question: For semiclassical Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials, does the violation of locality occur for generic potentials V, or only for specially chosen potentials?

evidence.quote: One may wonder whether the violation of locality holds for any generic choice of V or only for certain specially chosen ones.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the semiclassical Schrödinger operator
$$H_\hbar = -\hbar^2 \Delta + V(x) \quad \text{on } L^2(\mathbb{R}^d),$$
where $\hbar > 0$ is a small parameter and $V : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{C}$ is a (sufficiently regular, decaying) complex-valued potential. For a real potential, the Lieb–Thirring / Weyl-type bound on moments of negative eigenvalues
$$\sum_j |\lambda_j(H_\hbar)|^\gamma \le C_{\gamma,d}\, \hbar^{-d} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} (\operatorname{Re} V(x))_-^{\gamma + d/2}\, dx$$
expresses a form of "locality": the right-hand side depends only on the pointwise values of $V$, with the same constant valid for the whole class of potentials. One says that locality is *violated* for complex potentials if no inequality of the form
$$\sum_j \operatorname{dist}(\lambda_j(H_\hbar), [0,\infty))^\gamma \le C_{\gamma,d}\, \hbar^{-d} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} F(V(x))\, dx$$
(for any pointwise functional $F$ of $V$) can hold uniformly in $V$ in the semiclassical limit $\hbar \to 0$; equivalently, there exist sequences of complex potentials along which the eigenvalue sum is much larger than what Weyl's asymptotics for a corresponding local functional would predict.

It is known that there exist explicit complex-valued potentials $V$ for which such locality is violated. Determine whether this violation of locality is a *generic* phenomenon — for instance, whether it holds for a residual (dense $G_\delta$) or prevalent set of complex potentials $V$ in a natural function space — or whether, on the contrary, the violation occurs only for a meager (specially constructed) class of potentials, while for "most" complex $V$ a Weyl-type local bound on the eigenvalue sums still holds in the semiclassical limit.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly posed as one of three open problems in a 2024 note by Cuenin and Frank on violation of locality for Schrödinger operators with complex potentials. No subsequent work resolving the genericity question has been located.

status_evidence.title: Violation of locality for Schrödinger operators with complex potentials
status_evidence.snippet: We explain in which sense Schrödinger operators with complex potentials appear to violate locality (or Weyl's asymptotics), and we pose three open problems related to this phenomenon.
status_evidence.claim: The genericity-vs-special-potential question is posed as an open problem.
